info.name: Support Helpdesk API
info.description:
Every endpoint of the helpdesk API.

GETTING STARTED
1. Start the API: `php artisan serve --port=8080`
2. Run one of the three requests in `Sign in`. It stores the access token automatically, so every other request just works.
3. To act as a different role, run a different sign-in request.

The refresh token is an httpOnly cookie. Postman keeps it in its own cookie jar, so `Refresh session` works with no setup.

Access tokens last 10 minutes. If requests start returning 401 with `AUTH_TOKEN_STALE`, run `Refresh session` or sign in again.

SEEDED LOGINS (password `Passw0rd!` for all)
  admin@example.com    Amina Admin       admin
  sam@example.com      Sam Support       moderator
  priya@example.com    Priya Agent       moderator
  jordan@example.com   Jordan Employee   user
  dana@example.com     Dana Former       user, deactivated

EMAILS
Changing a status or assigning a ticket emails the person who raised it. With the default settings those messages are written to storage/logs/laravel.log, so `tail -f storage/logs/laravel.log` shows them with no mail server needed.

item.name: Sign in (one endpoint, five saved bodies)
item.description:
Every request in this folder is the same endpoint, POST /auth/login. They differ only in the credentials sent.

The first three store the access token, so running one is how you switch role. The last two show what failure looks like.

request.description:
Swaps the refresh cookie for a new access token and a new refresh cookie.

The old cookie stops working the moment it is used. Sending it twice means it leaked, so every session for that sign-in is ended.

originalRequest.description:

request.description: Ends this session only. Other devices stay signed in. Safe to call twice.

request.description:
Public. Always answers 202 with the same body whether or not the address has an account, so it cannot be used to find out who works here. If the account exists and is active, a one-time reset link is emailed. It expires after 60 minutes and a newer request retires any older link.

Rate limited: 5 per address and 10 per IP every 15 minutes.

response.name: Accepted

originalRequest.description:

Rate limited: 5 per address and 10 per IP every 15 minutes.

request.description:
Public. Takes the token and email from the link, plus the new password twice. On success the password changes, every existing session ends, and a confirmation email is sent.

400 RESET_LINK_INVALID covers every way a link can be bad (unknown, used, expired, wrong address) so the message reveals nothing. 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with field details for a weak or mismatched password.

request.description:
Agents and admins only.

Send `"assigneeId": null` to put it back in the queue. Leaving the field out means do not touch the assignment.

Only active agents can be assigned; anyone else is rejected with 422.

The person who raised the ticket is emailed when someone picks it up. Handing it back to the queue sends nothing.

request.description:
Agents and admins only. Can be combined with an assignment in the same request.

Allowed moves: open to in_progress, resolved or closed. in_progress to resolved or closed. resolved back to in_progress, or to closed. Closed is final.

Anything else returns 409. Changing the priority moves the deadline with it.

The person who raised the ticket is emailed when the status changes. Nobody is emailed about their own action.

request.description:
Admins only. Send any combination of name, email, role and active state.

Changing the role or deactivating signs the person out of every device on their next request. Correcting a name or email does not, because neither grants anything.

Two things are refused with 409, because either would lock the system: changing your own role or deactivating yourself, and removing the last active admin.

request.description:
Admins only. The account disappears from every list and can no longer sign in; every session ends at once. Their open and in-progress tickets go back to the queue unassigned. Resolved work and every comment keep their name, because the row is kept and only hidden.

409 for your own account and for the last active admin.
